claims.behaviour: The grid's keyboard shortcuts exist only on pages with the full grid: on the structure board and in gadgets they are active, on the Jira issue page panel and on the agile board tab no shortcut of the grid is bound at all. A key press is delivered as an action to the focused panel; when no panel has focus, to the panel under the event's target; otherwise to the widget as a whole. A key is swallowed only when its action reports it was handled; when an action is unavailable or declines, the key goes on to the browser and Jira.

Navigation keys in the grid: Up and `k` focus the row above; Down and `j` focus the row below; Left collapses the focused row or moves to its parent; Right expands the focused row or moves to the next row; PageUp and PageDown move a screen; Home and End go to the first and last displayed row; Escape and Shift+Escape cancel the current mode.

Selection keys in the grid: Space toggles the focused row's selection and moves down; Shift+Down, Shift+Up, Shift+PageUp, Shift+PageDown, Shift+Home and Shift+End move focus like the unshifted key and extend the selection; Shift+Right selects the focused row's subtree; Shift+Left deselects it; Ctrl+A on Windows and Linux, Cmd+A on Mac, toggles select all.

Expansion keys in the grid: Alt+`+`, Alt+`=` and Alt+Shift+`=` expand the next level; Alt+`-` collapses the next level; `+`,`+` or `=`,`=` (pressed in sequence, including Shift+`=` as either press) expand everything; `-`,`-` collapses everything; `=` or `+` followed by a digit 1 to 8, on the main keyboard or the numeric pad, is 'Expand N levels'.

Editing keys in the grid: F2 toggles edit mode; Tab and Shift+Tab go to the next and previous editable field; Ctrl+Alt+Up, Ctrl+Alt+Down, Ctrl+Alt+Left and Ctrl+Alt+Right go to the editable field in that direction; Enter adds an item below the focused row; Shift+Enter adds a child item; Alt+Enter adds an item above; Delete removes the selected rows with their subtrees; Insert creates a child item (not on Mac). In tooltips the edit-mode shortcut is written `F2` and the create-child shortcut is written as the formatted Insert key.
Move keys in the grid: Ctrl+Up moves the selection up, Ctrl+Down moves it down, Ctrl+Left outdents, Ctrl+Right indents. On Mac the same four actions also answer to Ctrl+Cmd with the arrow keys.

Clipboard and undo keys, on Windows and Linux: Ctrl+C copy; Ctrl+X and Shift+Delete cut; Ctrl+V and Shift+Insert paste; Ctrl+Shift+V and Shift+Alt+Insert paste under; Ctrl+Z undo; Ctrl+Shift+Z redo. On Mac Cmd replaces Ctrl for these (Cmd+C, Cmd+X, Cmd+V, Cmd+Shift+V, Cmd+Z, Cmd+Shift+Z), and the Shift+Delete and Insert combinations are not bound.

Two-key sequences in the grid (keys pressed one after the other): `i`,`i` view thumbnails; `v`,`v` select view; `v`,`s` save view; `v`,`s`,`s` save view as; `v`,`r` revert view; `v`,`v`,`v` previous view; `v`,`w` toggle text wrapping; `v`,`h` toggle horizontal scroll; `v`,`d` toggle the UI mode panel; `d`,`d` toggle the structure description; `q`,`q` quick transformations; `q` followed by 1 to 9 (main keyboard or numeric pad) toggles that quick transformation; `r`,`r` toggle unresolved; `s`,`s` open the structure selector; `s`,`q` open the action finder ('Find <product> action...'); `e`,`e` run all effectors; `t` followed by `=`, `+` or `t` adds a column; the sequence `i`,`d`,`d`,`q`,`d` opens a debugging action.

Layout, search and history keys: Ctrl+Alt+1, 2, 3, 4 (also on the numeric pad) switch to a single panel, the secondary panel, the details panel and the history panel; Alt+`\` swaps panels; `\` moves focus to the other panel; Ctrl+`]` shows an older history version and Ctrl+`[` a newer one; backquote and Shift+backquote toggle automation; Ctrl+Alt+`/` focuses search; Ctrl+Alt+`;` and Ctrl+Alt+Shift+`/` toggle the search filter; Ctrl+Alt+`[` and Ctrl+Alt+`]` go to the previous and next matching row; Ctrl+Alt+apostrophe toggles the query; Ctrl+Shift+`\` adds a column; on Mac also Cmd+`\` adds a column and Cmd+`]` toggles the UI mode panel.

Shortcuts that depend on where the grid runs. Everywhere the grid has shortcuts: Enter, Shift+Enter, Alt+Enter, `k`, `j`. Not in any gadget: Ctrl+`/` and Ctrl+Shift+`/` (show shortcuts) and `x` (manage saved columns). Everywhere except in the Confluence macro gadget: `o` open issue, Shift+`o` toggle the issue details without taking focus, `a` assign, `e` edit, `i` assign to me, `.` Jira actions, Alt+Down the row's actions menu, `m` comment, Ctrl+`.` pin, `z` full screen, and `g` is passed through to Jira so that its own `g` sequences keep working. `l` (labels) is bound outside gadgets and in the local gadget only.

Whether a grid action is enabled is recomputed for toolbar and menu controls 200 ms after a change: of the focused row, of the selection or of attribute data (for actions depending on them), of the clipboard or the fixed-view target issue (for paste), and when this panel becomes the focused panel. A focused-row change is ignored by a panel that is not the focused panel. When the panel lock or read-only state changes, every action is recomputed at once. Before an action is performed, its availability is checked again; if unavailable, nothing happens and the key is not swallowed.

While a column's configuration panel, the add-column panel or the UI mode panel is open, the panel is locked: arrow navigation, selection changes, row moves, editing, clipboard, deletion, bulk change, pinning and Jira actions do nothing. Jira-action shortcuts and 'open issue' still swallow the key while locked; the others let it through. Expand all, collapse all, expansion levels and the highlight commands are not blocked.

Down: with rows displayed, moves focus to the next displayed row, or to the first row when no row is focused. On the last row nothing happens and the key is not swallowed. With no rows displayed, nothing happens.
Up: moves focus to the previous displayed row. With no focused row, or on the first row, nothing happens and the key is not swallowed.

PageDown, given a focused row that is not the last: if the focused row is not the last row of the visible span, focus goes to the last visible row; if it already is, focus goes one screenful on, that is to index min(last index, to + (to - from + 1)). Example: 100 rows, visible span 10 to 29, focus on 15 gives 29; focus on 29 gives 49.

PageUp, given a focused row that is not the first: if the focused row is not the first of the visible span, focus goes to the first visible row; if it already is, focus goes to index max(0, from - (to - from + 1)). Example: visible span 40 to 59, focus on 45 gives 40; focus on 40 gives 20.
Home moves focus to the first displayed row and End to the last, only when a row is focused and it is not already there. Otherwise nothing happens and the key is not swallowed.
Every focus move from the keyboard is followed by making the focused row visible, at most once in 250 ms.

The Shift variants of Down, Up, PageDown, PageUp, Home and End follow the same target rules as the plain keys and ask the selection model to extend the selection along the way. With no focused row, Shift+Down still focuses the first row.

'Select subtree' (Shift+Right), 'Deselect subtree' (Shift+Left) and 'Select to the root' act on the expanded forest through the selection model and do nothing when the panel is locked. In either case the key is not swallowed.

Escape does the first of these that applies and then stops: (1) cancels a mouse drag in progress; (2) offers the event to the element with keyboard focus, and if that element or a parent cancels it (for instance a banner closing itself), stops; (3) closes the current popup; (4) cancels the current cell edit; (5) hides the cell overflow hint; (6) clears the selection, when rows are explicitly selected. If none applies the key is not swallowed.
Left: with a focused row that is expanded and has children, collapses it and keeps it visible; otherwise moves focus to its parent row. With no parent or no focused row nothing happens.

Right: with a focused row that has children and is collapsed, expands it and keeps it visible; otherwise moves focus to the next row, like Down. With no focused row, focuses the first row if there is one.

'Expand all' and 'Collapse all' change every row's state. If the focused row was visible before, it is scrolled back into view right after, on the next tick; if it was not visible the scroll position is left alone.

'Expand next level' raises the expansion level by 1 and 'Collapse next level' lowers it by 1; both then keep the focused row visible. The shortcut 'Expand N levels' (N from 1 to 8) sets the expansion level to N - 1, so 'Expand 1 level' is level 0. An action call with a `level` argument sets that level; a missing or negative level does nothing.

When expansion changes and the focused row is no longer displayed, focus moves to its nearest ancestor that is displayed and that row is scrolled into view. If none is displayed focus is left as it is.

'Next matching' and 'Previous matching' walk the expanded forest from the focused row in that direction and focus the first row that matches the current highlight, without wrapping. With no focused row, 'Next matching' starts at the first row and 'Previous matching' finds nothing. During cell editing they do nothing and the key is not swallowed. With no active highlight, or no further match, they report handled and focus stays.

Going to the closest match (used by search) does nothing during cell editing or with no active highlight. With no focused row it behaves as 'Next matching'. With a focused row that matches it stays. With one that does not it goes to the next match, and when no later row matches focus stays: the search backwards is never reached (as the original does).
Space: with a focused row, toggles that row's selection and then moves focus down one row as Down does. With no focused row nothing happens.
Select all: with a focused row, toggles between all rows selected and none. With no focused row nothing happens: the key is not swallowed and the browser's own select-all applies.

A plain click on a row's selection mark toggles that row's selection and makes the panel the focused panel, without following a link. A click on it with Shift and no other modifier is suppressed here and left to the mouse selection logic. A click on the select-all mark in the header toggles select all.

Clicking a thumbnail in a thumbnail field cell opens the image gallery for that cell instead of following the link. 'View thumbnails' (`i`,`i`) needs a focused row and a column of the field `thumbnail` in the view: it scrolls the focused row into view and opens the first thumbnail of that row, if it has one. Without such a column the key is not swallowed.

The rows a move, indent or outdent acts on are the selected rows, or the focused row when nothing is selected; or the row of the new-item details editor, when one is active. They are refused as a whole when the panel is read-only, when the first row lies on a pinned item's root path, or when several rows are selected that are not consecutive siblings at one depth with nothing else selected between them.

Move item up is available when the first moved row has a preceding sibling and the forest allows the move under the current parent. It places the rows before that sibling, keeping the parent: the request's `after` is the sibling before that one, or 0 at the start. The action name recorded is `move-up` and the focused row is kept visible.

Move item down is available when the last moved row has a following sibling and the forest allows the move under the current parent. It places the rows after that sibling. The action name recorded is `move-down` and the focused row is kept visible.

Indent is available when the first moved row has a preceding sibling at its depth (not on the first row, and not when the row above is shallower) and the forest allows the rows under that sibling. It expands the sibling and moves the rows there, after its last child. The action name recorded is `level-down`; the focused row is kept visible.

Outdent is available when the first moved row is not at the top level, its parent is not on a pinned item's root path, and the forest allows the rows under the grandparent (the top level when there is none). The rows are placed directly after their old parent. The action name recorded is `level-up`; the focused row is kept visible.

F2 outside editing is available when a row is focused, the panel is not read-only and the row is known to be editable. It opens the editor in the column last edited, when that column is still in the view and editable for this row; if the row has upload errors and that column has none, the first cell with an error is used; otherwise the main column. During editing F2 finishes all edits. A control for this action shows as toggled while an editor is active.
Tab outside any cell editor behaves as F2 outside editing; Shift+Tab outside any cell editor does nothing and is not swallowed.

Tab in a cell editor goes to the next editable column of the row (Shift+Tab, previous), skipping columns not editable for it. Past the end of the row: if the row is not ready to finish (for instance a new item that still needs its main field) the editor goes to the main column. Otherwise it goes to the first (Shift+Tab, last) editable column of the next (previous) displayed row, if that row is known to be editable; if none, all edits finish. Tab is always swallowed while an editor is open.

Ctrl+Alt+Left and Ctrl+Alt+Right in a cell editor go to the nearest editable column in that direction in the same row. At the row's end they stay where they are and still swallow the key. Outside an editor they do nothing.

Ctrl+Alt+Up and Ctrl+Alt+Down in a cell editor move to the same column in the nearest displayed row in that direction that is editable, trying at most 100 rows, and stay put if none opens. If the current row is not ready to finish, the editor goes to its main column instead.

The grid has commands, without keys of their own here, to finish all edits, cancel the current row's edit ('Cancel issue edit'), cancel the current cell edit ('Cancel edit'), revert the current cell's edit, and switch the current edit to the full Jira dialog; each delegates to the item editor.

Create actions and what each does at the focused row: 'Create' (Enter) sibling below with a type choice; 'Create child' (Insert) and Shift+Enter child; 'Create above' (Alt+Enter) sibling above; 'Create issue', 'Create folder', memo, planning task, 'Add Confluence page' and each generic item type registered by another app: sibling below of that type. 'Create under' is a sibling issue below; 'Create with dialog' is the same through Jira's create dialog; a further command creates a sibling folder below, and another a sibling page with the preset whose name carries a small 'try' badge.

A create action is available only when the panel shows a structure, is neither locked nor read-only, Jira's configuration allows issue creation (this condition applies to every item type) and the new row's position is allowed by the forest. 'Create with dialog' also needs the dialog to be possible.

Where a new row goes. Child: under the focused row, first (`after` 0). Sibling below: under the focused row's parent, after it. Above: under the parent, before it. With no focused row: under the last pinned root path's last row, or the top level with no pin; at the start for 'above' and at the end otherwise; if the pin matched no paths at all, the action is unavailable. A focused title row, or the pinned row itself, forces child placement. A focused row above the pinned row is refused.

A new item's sample for pre-filling fields: walking back from the focused row through preceding siblings and then parents, the first row that is an issue gives the issue sample, and the nearest planning task on the way gives the planning sample. Each sample holds the item id and the row id. Rows that cannot be used stop the walk.

Performing a create: if the active editor has tabs and nothing was typed yet, the action only switches to the tab of the requested type and takes focus. Otherwise a temporary negative row id is allocated, the current focused path is remembered, the parent is expanded, a new-item editor opens there, focus is forced to the new row and it is scrolled into view. If the edit is cancelled and that row was still focused, focus returns to the remembered path and is scrolled into view.
When temporary row ids are replaced by real ones after upload, the remembered focused path follows the new ids.

Copy is available unless the panel shows the clipboard, is locked, or a selected row has no real id yet. From a key press it also steps aside when the page has selected text, leaving the browser to copy it. It needs at least one copyable row. Copy places the selected rows with the panel on the clipboard.
Cut is available under the same rules as copy, except that a read-only panel also refuses it and selected page text does not matter, and it uses the cut set of rows.

Paste needs a panel that is neither locked nor read-only, a non-empty clipboard and a position the forest can merge at. Position: after the focused row (top level with none). 'Paste under' needs a focused row and places rows as last children. A paste landing at the top level of a panel with a title row turns into paste under. A position above a pinned row is refused when a row is focused; with no focused row it goes under the last root path's last row.

Paste expands the target for 'Paste under'. A cut pasted directly after its own first row clears the clipboard and does nothing else. A cut whose source is the same forest specification is a move (action name `paste`), and focus goes to the first moved row. Anything else is a merge of the clipboard forest, passing where a cut came from and, for a copy, whether source and target are the same untransformed forest; focus goes to the first new row that is displayed, or else to the row before the position. On a refused request focus is unchanged.

Removing rows is available when the panel is neither locked nor read-only, something is selected or focused, and for each row (at most the first 100 when only computing availability, all of them before performing) the row is not above a pinned row and the forest allows removing it. The rows acted on are the selection normalised to top-most rows.

Removing rows: edits in the removed subtrees are cancelled first, and if one cannot be cancelled nothing is removed. Rows already gone are skipped. The server is asked to delete with action name `remove`, and the removed subtrees go to the deleted-items store. If focus was in a removed subtree it moves to the next row after the removal. The message counts all rows in the subtrees.

After a removal an auto-closing warning flag appears for 5 seconds with the text 'You have removed an item from the structure.' for one row and 'You have removed N items from the structure.' for more, with the words after 'You have' in bold, and, if undo is possible, a second line with the action link 'Undo Remove' which performs undo.

Bulk change is available when the panel is not locked, Jira allows bulk change and at least 2 selected rows are issues. It leaves the page by POST (same window) to `/secure/StructureBulkChange.jspa` with `issues` the issue ids joined with single spaces, `homeUrl` the current page URL and `atl_token` the page's token.

'Convert selected planning tasks' is available whenever the panel is not locked and opens the effector process dialog with module key `com.almworks.jira.structure:effector-conversion`, `selectedItems` the item ids of the selected planning-task rows (possibly none) and forest spec `{structureId}`.

'Run all effectors' (`e`,`e`) applies when effectors may run here and the forest has at least one effector row. It opens the effector process dialog with all effector ids of the panel's forest data and the structure id. Otherwise the key is not swallowed.

Pin (Ctrl+`.`) does nothing when the panel is locked, automation is on or history is showing. With a pinned item it unpins. Otherwise it needs a focused real row and pins the anchor issue of the page, if the page has one (as a string), or else the focused row's item id.
'Insert current issue' adds the page's anchor issue after the focused row, or at the top of the forest with no focused row. Without an anchor issue it is unavailable.

`o` with no details panel configured: for a focused real row with a key, saves the navigation hint cookie and goes to the issue URL, in the parent window when in a gadget and in this window otherwise. When Jira actions are disabled here (remote or macro gadget, agile tab) the action does nothing.

`o` where the page has the issue details panel and this is the primary panel: toggles the details panel and moves focus into it. It is available when details are on or the focused row is valid for them, and shows as toggled while details are on. When the panel is locked the key is swallowed with no effect.
The navigation hint is cookie `structure3.navigation.hint` with value `<structure id>|<millis now>|<issue key>`, 1 day, on the Jira cookie path. It is only written while a structure is open.

The Jira row shortcuts need a focused real row that is known to be editable; without one the key is not swallowed. When the panel is locked, or this is the primary panel, the details panel is showing without being able to interact, and the row is an issue, they swallow the key and do nothing.

On the board, `a` and `l` on an issue row open Jira's own assign and labels dialogs, if Jira provides them, with Jira's assign or label action link as the trigger. On a non-issue row the key is not swallowed.
On the board, `e` on an issue row with a real issue id clicks Jira's edit-issue action; on a non-issue row it opens the in-grid editor in the main column.
On the board, `m` opens Jira's comment dialog on an issue row. Where the details panel is configured and visible and has a comment button in its footer, that button is clicked instead, for any row.
`i` on the board clicks the first Jira assign-to-me action link on the page, if any, and always swallows the key, with no check of the row or lock (as the original does).

Alt+Down opens the actions-column menu of the focused row, when that row has its trigger on screen. If the panel is locked it swallows the key; otherwise, with no real focused row or no trigger, it does not.

In the local gadget the assign, edit, assign-to-me, comment and labels shortcuts work by navigation: for a focused editable issue row, they take the matching link template from the gadget's hidden issue-action links, replace `id={0}` with the issue id, add `returnUrl` with the top window's URL and send the top window (the same-origin one) there. Templates without `id={0}` are ignored. In a remote or macro gadget and on the agile tab none of the Jira actions is registered.

'Next duplicate' and 'Previous duplicate' move focus to the next or previous row of the expanded forest whose item has duplicates, wrapping around past the end, and force focus onto the row. The search starts after the focused row. With no focused row, going back starts from the last row, and going forward starts from the second row and never looks at the first (as the original does). They are never reported as handled.
'Search and Add' switches to the two-panel layout, sets the secondary panel to the search-and-add specification, focuses that panel and puts the cursor in its query field.
'Find <product> action...' (`s`,`q`) opens the action finder for this panel, at any time.

Other grid features can ask to focus a row; to walk rows up or down to the first row passing a test, optionally wrapping; to toggle the pin; and to list the editable columns of a row, which are the columns of the view that are editable and not known to be non-editable for that issue.

The column header has one cell per column of the view, in view order. Each is labelled for screen readers '<column name> column'. Every cell can take keyboard focus except those of the handle and actions columns. Every column after the first has a pin indicator and a sort indicator next to its name.

While a header cell has keyboard focus the widget's shortcuts are off and its controls are showing; they come back on blur. Releasing Down or Enter on a focused header cell opens that column's configuration panel.

Header controls (name overlay, configure caret, resize handles) are hidden until the mouse hovers over the header, with hover intent sampled every 50 ms and a 500 ms delay on leaving. They fade in over 100 ms and out over 200 ms. They stay up without fading while a column is being resized or dragged, a configuration panel is open, or a header cell has focus, and vanish at once when such a state ends with the mouse away.

The column whose controls are highlighted is, in order of priority: the one with keyboard focus; the one being dragged; the one being configured; otherwise the one under the mouse, or none when the pointer is within 2.5 px of a column boundary or beyond the last column. Nothing is highlighted during a resize or with the controls hidden. With the add-column or UI mode panel open only the first two apply.

A resize handle activates when the pointer is within 2.5 px of a boundary between two columns; during a resize it stays on the handle being dragged. No handle activates while a column is dragged or any configuration panel is open. The header cell of the column that will change is marked as well, if that column is resizable: the column left of the boundary when that is before the stretching column, otherwise the column right of it.

There are one fewer resize handles than columns; handle i sits between columns i and i+1. With no stretching column it can move only if both columns are resizable. With one at index s it can move if column i is resizable, for i < s, and if column i+1 is resizable, for i >= s. A handle that cannot move does nothing on drag or double-click.

Dragging a resize handle moves horizontally inside the header and shows an indicator line down the grid. While dragging, the other columns are previewed live at the widths they would get. Normally only one column changes: the column left of the handle when the handle is before the stretching column, otherwise the column right of it; with no stretching column both change, one growing as the other shrinks. On release the indicator disappears and the new explicit widths are saved through the view.
Modifiers during a resize drag. Alt, only when horizontal scrolling is off: both columns next to the handle change and snapping is off. Ctrl or Cmd: snapping is off.

A resize stops at each adjacent column's minimum width: the handle cannot go further and the opposite column absorbs the difference. A column's minimum is its own; if it is the last column of the view and not the actions column, the minimum is 64 px more.

With snapping on, a resize drag within 15 px of the width the column would naturally have (its stretched width, else preferred width, else default width) snaps to that width. When a drop lands snapped, the column's explicit width is cleared so that it follows its natural width, except when the view scrolls horizontally or columns are over-allocated, in which case the natural width is stored as explicit; a right-hand column stores it only when over-allocated.
Resizing is refused while the layout has not been computed yet, or when columns cannot fit even at their minimum widths.

Width calculation works on two groups. Scrollable columns are those in the horizontally scrolling part when that mode is on; fixed columns are all the others. The available width is the grid area's client width; below 20 px no calculation is done and when the grid is hidden the previous one stays. The default for a column with no width of its own is its default width, or its minimum, or 16 px.

A scrollable column's width is its explicit width, else its preferred width capped at 350 px, else its default. The room for fixed columns is the available width minus the scrollable columns' total, where that total is counted as at most 30% of the available width (rounded).

A fixed column's width is its explicit width; else, when the available width has not changed since the last calculation or a resize is under way, its last stretched width; else its preferred width; else its default. A column with a preferred width above an equal share of the room left for fixed columns is a flexible column, and so is the stretching column when the total is under the available width or horizontal scrolling is off.

Extra room is first given to the scrollable part up to its need. When fixed columns then overflow, flexible columns drop to their minimum (non-stretching ones not below the equal share). When there is room left, flexible columns grow in equal parts, those with a preferred width stopping there.

If columns still overflow, the excess is taken from non-stretching fixed resizable columns in turn: first proportionally from columns above their natural width, towards it; then proportionally towards each column's minimum (never under 16 px). Outside a resize preview it then takes from columns that allow shrinking when out of space, and finally from all resizable columns, down to 16 px. If it still does not fit, a warning is logged and the grid overflows.

When widths are applied to the header, if the last column's width plus the vertical scrollbar's width is under 64 px, the last header cell is widened to reach 64 px, reducing the cells to its left from right to left. Header cells of columns scrolled out of view are drawn reduced by the scroll offset and limited to the room left beside the fixed ones.

Widths are recomputed when columns or column widths change, and on each layout change at most once per 100 ms. A layout change retries up to 10 times, at 100 ms intervals, while the width is below 20 px or the grid's client width still equals its outer width (no scrollbar measured yet), the latter except on Mac WebKit with overlay scrollbars. Showing or hiding the actions-column menu also recomputes.
Column widths are applied by one per-panel style, and other parts of the grid are told of a resize only when some width changed.

The horizontal scroll offset of the grid is bound to the grid area's own scroll and never exceeds total column width minus visible width. It is saved to the view before the page may unload and before a view switch, and restored when columns change with a request to do so. The grid shows a hint of more content on the left when the offset is above 0, and on the right when offset + visible width + 1 is below the total.
On Internet Explorer, which the pinned Jira does not support, a separate scrollbar below the rows moves the scrollable part. A replacement need not keep this.

Double-clicking a column's name resets that column to its natural width, if it is resizable; double-clicking a movable resize handle resets the column left of it, if the handle is before the main column, and the column right of it, if at or after the main column. With Alt, or with no main column, both are reset. Double-clicking the main column's name, or a non-resizable column's, gives no column to reset, and the empty request resets all columns' manual widths.

A button titled 'Autosize all columns' clears every manual column width on click or on Enter. It appears when the first column is at least 49 px wide (always in the remote gadget), positioned just inside its right edge. While it has keyboard focus the widget's shortcuts are off.

The header has a select-all mark titled 'Select all items', except in the remote gadget. Enter on it while focused clicks it. While it has keyboard focus the widget's shortcuts are off. It shows all, some or none selected.

A click on a column name sorts by that column after 500 ms, unless a second click follows inside that time, which cancels it. Automation mode blocks sorting. A column without a sort transform does nothing. Clicks on the main column instead remove all sort transforms from the panel.

Clicking a column that is not yet a current sort sorts in the column's default direction. Clicking a column already sorted reverses it. A current sort matches when the column's sorter and the transform have the same module and parameters, ignoring `id`, `key` and the parameters `desc`, `from`, `to` and `locale`.

A plain click on a column replaces all other sorts with this one, keeping non-sorting transforms: a current sort is updated in place, a new one is appended. Shift+click, or a click with no transforms at all, saves it as an additional transform (a further sort level).

The header shows an ascending or descending indicator on the column whose sort transform is in the panel's transforms, updated when the panel's specification changes. With automation on no sort shows as active.
The header shows the pin indicator on columns in the fixed part while the view scrolls horizontally, updated when columns change.

Dragging a column name reorders columns. Only horizontal movement counts. A label with the column's name follows the mouse. The handle, actions and blank columns cannot be dragged and cannot be crossed: a drop is limited to the last place before such a column. An indicator shows the drop place; the place is decided by the middle of the dragged label against each column's middle. A drop on either side of the column itself does nothing.

Reordering across the pinned boundary: dropping an unpinned column on a pinned column pins it; dropping a pinned column on an unpinned one unpins it. The main column cannot be unpinned, so it is not moved, and with horizontal scrolling on the UI marks the drag as prohibited while it is over such a place. Statistics recorded: `view.moveColumnWithPin`, `view.moveColumnWithUnpin`, and `view.moveColumn` after any move.

A reorder gives the view the moved column id, the ids of columns before and after its new place, and whether it landed in the pinned part. If a column's configuration panel is open it then follows to the new index.

Where the configuration allows it, the header has a button titled 'Add a column', also the 'Add column' action. A click opens the add-column panel; a click while that panel is open closes it. A loading state shows if the panel is not ready after 300 ms. The button shows as pressed while the panel is open. Clicking outside the panel closes it.

When a column is chosen in the add-column panel the panel closes, the column goes through the view (passing the current column ids and any temporary ones), the grid scrolls to the far right, and statistics are recorded. If the column wants configuring, its configuration panel opens 100 ms later.

Adding a column records `view.addColumn`, and with a column key also `view.addColumn.<key>`. For key `field` it then records `view.addColumn.field.custom` for custom fields or `view.addColumn.field.<field id>`; for key `attribute`, `view.addColumn.attribute.<attribute id>`. When such a column has no field or attribute parameter, `view.addColumn.<key>` is recorded a second time (as the original does).

Each column except handle, actions and blank has a caret titled 'Configure this column' opening the column's configuration panel beside it; a second click closes it, and a loading state shows after 300 ms. The panel is told whether the column is the main column. If the panel cannot load the column it closes. Clicking outside closes it, and opening one configuration panel closes any other.

When the column configuration panel reports a change, the column is updated through the view only if the column still exists, is not handle, actions or blank, and its specification really differs; `view.changeColumn` is recorded. Removal applies only to such a column that is not the main column; `view.removeColumn` is recorded and the panel closes.

While a configuration panel is open the rest of the grid is covered so that it cannot be used: for the add-column and UI mode panels the whole grid; for a column's panel everything except that column, which stays visible and follows its resizing.
Opening a configuration panel and closing the last one are announced to other grid parts, and popups are told so that they close each other. Clicking an item link in the grid closes the panels.

Where the configuration allows it, the header has a button titled 'Configure UI mode', opening the UI mode panel, also the toggle action of `v`,`d`. It shows as pressed while open, and clicking outside closes it.
The action 'manage saved columns' (`x`, or the entry of the add-column panel, which closes that panel first) opens the saved columns dialog, loading it on first use.
The header marks the column whose cell is being edited, and removes the mark when no editor is active.
After a column change that asks for it, the resize handles of chosen resizable columns flash once, to show which columns were adjusted.
For a row drag the header provides an empty copy of the grid's sections at current width and scroll, on which the dragged rows are drawn.

Row height in single-line mode is 33 px. The grid's content height is the larger of the rows' total height (plus any drop gap) and the minimum height, which is 2 rows (66 px), plus the height needed by an active taller editor, plus the footer extra space when there is any.

Only a window of rows is in the page. With the visible span from `from` to `to`, let n = max(to - from, 10): the window is kept while it covers [from - n, to + n], clipped to the forest. When it does not, the new window is [from - 3n, to + 3n], clipped; if it holds fewer than 50 rows it is widened to 50, half of the shortfall before it. Example: forest 1000, visible span 100 to 120: n = 20, needed 80 to 140, new window 40 to 180. Visible span 0 to 5: n = 10, needed 0 to 15, new window 0 to 50.

Only rows in the window are in the page; rows that leave it are taken out and may come back from the row cache, and rows that stay are not moved. Attribute subscriptions follow the rows in the window plus the ancestors of its first row. After a rebuild the grid's focus is put back; if the element that had keyboard focus lost it, it gets it again, and if that element is inside a cell editor panel the focused row is scrolled into view.
On scroll the window is recomputed 50 ms later. The scroll position is remembered 1 second after scrolling stops, with the same delay after any layout change.
When the displayed forest changes, the window is rebuilt once the current event round finishes, and the update is then announced so that changed rows repaint.

Scrolling a row into view: if the row top is outside the viewport, or the row is taller than the viewport, it goes to the top of the viewport; if its bottom overflows, it goes to the bottom. If already fully visible, nothing moves and its place is remembered. A row being edited counts as at least as tall as its editor. A row that is not displayed is ignored.

Scrolling a row into view at a given fraction, in single-line mode: the row is placed at round(fraction x (viewport - 33)) from the viewport top, with the scroll offset clamped so that the grid does not end above the viewport bottom.
Setting the grid's scroll to a fraction f: offset = round(f x (rows x 33 - viewport height)), limited to the content; 0 when all rows fit.
Requests to keep the focused row visible are limited to one per 250 ms. Scrolling requested before the first rows are in the page is applied when the first rows arrive.

Each row shows state that a test can see in its element: expanded, collapsed or leaf; focused; cut or copied (when its row is on the clipboard, never in the clipboard panel); being dragged; root row or on the root path when an item is pinned; history status while history is showing; being edited. Rows not matching the active highlight are dimmed, the focused row never.

A row's selection mark shows selected, or auto-selected (selected because of its parent). For a collapsed row with children the mark also tells whether all, some or none of its hidden subtree is selected; a selected collapsed row with no selected descendants is marked as such. The header's select-all mark shows all when explicitly selected rows equal the forest size, and some when any is selected.
When focus moves, only the old and new focused rows repaint their state. A focus move that asks for it also scrolls into view.
When the highlight changes, every row in the window recomputes its dimmed state.

A row marked as about to change flashes on the next window rebuild. A marked row that leaves the window plays the flash out and then goes away. Each finished flash is announced. Marked rows are dropped when the panel's forest specification changes.
Clicking a row's upload error icon opens the pending decision popup.
Clicking a row's duplicate icon focuses the row and toggles the pin, and goes no further.
With horizontal scrolling off, all columns are in one section and the left and right sections are hidden from screen readers; with it on they are exposed. Changing the mode rebuilds the window.
For screen readers each row is a row with a 1-based row index, each cell a grid cell labelled '<column name> column', and the row list has a row count equal to the expanded forest size.

When the multi-selection banner opens, the grid scrolls down by 51 px, except when a selected row lies within the top 51 px of the viewport. When it closes, the grid scrolls up by 51 px if more than 51 px remain below the viewport.

A cell editor taller than the rows below it extends the grid to 33 x row index + editor height. Growth is immediate, and so is shrinking when no extension is in effect. Otherwise shrinking starts 5 seconds after the need falls and takes 800 ms. A new need cancels a pending shrink.

Extra space requested below the rows is added to the content height, less the height taken by the horizontal scrollbar; while the request is above 0, that height is re-measured 1 second after a column resize.

Each row keeps one cached set of elements, one per section, for the row id. The cache holds 250 rows and never evicts a row on the page. A row is painted again only when forced, or when its data sequence (the larger of row and attribute data sequences) has changed since the last paint.
A requested repaint of a row is batched and happens 25 ms later, unless it is asked to be immediate. A row that is not cached is not painted.
An issue row's element carries the issue id in `rel`, so that Jira's issue features can find it.

The grid always asks the server for attributes `key` (format `text`), `summary` (`text`) and `editable` (`boolean`), plus `project` and `issuetype` (`id`) unless Jira forbids creating issues, and every column's required attributes. A column failing to name them is logged and skipped. On a column change, off-page rows are dropped from the cache and all remaining rows repaint.

Rows repaint when attribute data arrives, when a row changes in the displayed forest, and when a row's expansion changes. A displayed row that cannot be repainted because it is not in the forest or not subscribed logs a warning and keeps its old content.

When temporary row ids are replaced by real ones for the panel's untransformed specification, the cached elements of each row move to the new id, unless the new id already has elements, and row attributes follow.
Painting a row fills one cell per column of each section, in order, and removes surplus cells. A column whose rendering throws leaves its cell empty and logs a warning; other cells are not affected.

Cells whose column allows it show the loading placeholder in two cases. A row not ready to render yet shows it in those cells (the main column inside its empty layout) and leaves other cells empty. In a ready row, a cell shows it when every value the column read is still absent. It never shows on a temporary row, a row being edited or an inaccessible row.
On a repaint of a row on the page: a cell whose editor reports an error flashes as an error; otherwise a cell whose column says the value changed flashes as changed.
A cell painted with a value the server marked as outdated is marked as outdated.
The main column's depth offset for a row is 32 px per level plus 12 px. In a panel with a title row, depth counts one less, not below 0.
A column may ask for its row to be repainted when an asynchronous result ends, which works only while the result is pending.
The loading placeholder is a row of 80 bullets with the tooltip 'Loading...'.

After 500 ms of hovering a loading placeholder, its bullets start animating, up to 80 of them or as many as fit. Moving away stops it at the end of the current cycle; hovering a section header stops it at once. If the bullet width cannot be measured, the animation is off for that panel from then on.

Rows wrap text when the view's text wrapping is on and the layout is single panel, two panels or details; in other layouts, or with it off, rows are one line. On a mode change the row and offset at the viewport's anchor are kept. The anchor is the focused row, if its top or bottom is in the viewport; otherwise the first row fully in view.

In one-line mode: row y = index x 33; the first visible row index is floor(pxfrom / 33) and the last ceil(pxto / 33) - 1, both clamped to the rows, the last not before the first. A y position during a drag gives row floor(y / 33). The anchor row is ceil(pxfrom / 33) when it exists.

When the mouse enters a row in one-line mode, each non-empty cell is checked: it overflows if its value is wider than the cell content width minus half the fade area (and minus the expander, in the main column) or taller than 33 px. Overflowing cells then offer the 'more' hint control, until the mouse leaves the row.

In text wrapping mode each row in the window is measured and its height remembered by row id; rows not yet measured count as 33 px. Row positions are the sums of those heights. A row's parts in all sections get the height of its tallest part when horizontal scrolling is on; with it off they are as tall as their content.

In text wrapping mode rows are remeasured when columns are resized and when horizontal scrolling is turned on. A row whose content changed is remeasured only if its height was known. Turning horizontal scrolling off removes the forced heights. After remeasuring, the anchor row is kept in place.

In text wrapping mode remeasuring is suspended while the user scrolls by dragging the scrollbar or by the mouse wheel, so that the scrollbar does not jump; rows not measured yet stay on one line meanwhile. It resumes 2500 ms after the mouse button is released or the last wheel event, and then remeasures all rows in the window.

In text wrapping mode, when a row drag starts all rows go to one line, the drag's reference row staying where it was: if needed, a gap is put above the rows and scrolling goes to 0. The gap counts in all row positions. When the drag stops the 2500 ms delay runs and then normal measuring and anchoring come back.
Leaving text wrapping mode forgets all measured heights, removes forced heights from cached rows and ends any freeze.

The row under the mouse is highlighted as hovered, except the focused row. Hover changes only when the pointer really moves, and not during a column resize or a row drag. Leaving a row clears it unless the pointer goes to the overflow hint. Any key release clears it.
With the mouse idle for 5 seconds, the hover highlight fades out slowly, checked every 500 ms; a row reached with the mouse idle that long is not highlighted.
While history is showing, a row displays its status for the chosen version: added, moved to, moved from, removed or copied.

For each change of the chosen history version the grid shows, on all sections, a bracket around the changed rows that are displayed: a start mark at their top and an end mark at their bottom. Added and copied rows, and moved rows after the change, use the 'to' look; the rest use the 'from' look. For a move, a line marks the other position: where the rows go, before the change; where they came from, after it.

A change with no displayed rows is shown only by position lines: add or copy, a 'to' line; remove, a 'from' line; move, both. A position is the row after the closest displayed preceding sibling's subtree, or after the closest displayed parent, or the top of the grid when neither exists. Marks that would overlap are moved by a pixel or two to stay apart, and stay inside the content.

Going to a history change first expands the ancestors of the changed rows and all collapsed changed rows with children, for every change of the version. Then it scrolls to the first change's displayed rows: nothing if they are fully in view; centred if they fit in the viewport; top-aligned if not. If none are displayed it scrolls to the position line, keeping one row (33 px) of margin, or not at all if the line is in view.

During a row drag the grid opens a gap at the drop position: the gap grows at the new position over 300 ms with a cosine curve, sampled every 30 ms, while gaps at earlier positions close at the same rate. A row that already has a gap continues from it. Clearing the drag closes all gaps at once.

Over an overflowing cell's 'more' control, the hint appears after 1 second of hovering, or at once on click. While a hint is open for a column, moving to another row's overflowing cell in that column switches the hint at once; moving to another cell starts the 500 ms closing delay. No hint opens during cell editing.

An open hint closes 500 ms after the mouse leaves it or the section, unless it comes back to the hint; it fades out in 50 ms, and fades in in 50 ms. It also closes at once on a click elsewhere on the board, on the close button of the summary hint, when editing starts, on horizontal scrolling, and on Escape. Clicks inside the hint and on a 'more' control do not close it.

The hint for the main column has a header with the row's icon, its full name and a close button, and below it the row's extra attributes shown in the cell, each with its label when it has one: 'Lead', 'Start date', 'End date', 'Release date'. The description is shown as a block; for a version row the aggregated description is shown. A row type with an unknown layout gives no hint and a warning is logged.

The hint for other columns: an icons cell gets a copy of the cell's content at natural width. Others are measured at 255 px wide: when wider than 255 px, or taller than 23 px, or containing code, it is a multi-line hint, at least 255 px wide; otherwise a single-line hint at the cell's width.

A hint opens at the cell, 2 px below its top, and is kept within the grid: moved left and up to fit, and if taller than the grid it is cut to the grid's height and scrolls inside itself, and that scrolling does not scroll the page. A main column hint is narrower than the cell by 48 px, a multi-line one by 10 px, and neither below 255 px.
While a hint is open, its column's header cell widens to show the full column name, staying within the grid, and returns to its width when the hint closes.
If building a hint fails, it stays closed and a warning is logged.

A panel started with no specification, once the widget is initialised and the panel visible, loads a default: the primary panel an empty JQL query, specification `{sQuery: {type: "jql", query: ""}}`; other panels the search-and-add specification.

For a structure, the panel loads its properties with `GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}`, with no query parameters, and keeps them for the life of the page per structure id, until the client learns the structure was updated. The answer counts only if its `id` equals the requested one, otherwise nothing changes. On an error the panel has no properties, if it still shows that structure.

A panel not showing a structure gets local properties. Name: 'Clipboard' for the clipboard, 'Trash' for the trash; 'Query' for a query; 'Unknown Structure' otherwise. It is read-only exactly when it shows the clipboard. With no specification it has no properties.
A panel is read-only when it has no properties, when the properties say `readOnly`, or when the whole widget is forced read-only.
Until the panel's forest first loads, it shows a loading placeholder instead of the rows, and the column header stays visible.

When the forest answered and the panel has no structure properties, the rows are replaced with 'Sorry, structure with ID <id> does not exist or you don't have permissions to view it.' and the column header is hidden. This also shows if the forest arrives first, until the properties do.

With a pinned item not found in the forest and automation off, the rows are replaced with 'The pinned item is not found in this structure.' and a link 'Remove Pin' that unpins, and the column header is hidden.
The panel's content height is the grid's height, or the message's height when a message replaces rows, and never under 2 rows.

Before a panel changes what it shows, unsaved work is checked. With uncommitted edits or new items a browser confirmation opens with 'Some of the item edits were not uploaded. If you close this structure now, those changes will be lost.', a blank line, 'Changed: <list>', the list being changed item names plus 'one new item' or 'N new items'. If uploads are blocked, a further paragraph of two sentences says that some changes wait because creating a new item failed, and what to do. With only pending uploads the text is 'We're still uploading changes to the server. If you leave this page now, some of the changes you've made may be lost.'
Declining that confirmation keeps the panel as it is. Accepting it cancels all edits, clears the panel's row state and clears its upload queue, and the change goes ahead.
A specification can be changed without a question only if there are no uncommitted edits, no new items and no blocked uploads.

Which forest a panel asks for. With automation on or history showing, `pinnedItem` and `transforms` are left out of the specification; otherwise the panel's pinned item follows the specification. With automation on, not in history, for a structure, it asks for `title: true`. With history showing for a structure and a chosen version of that structure, it asks for that `version`. An invalid specification means no forest.

Unless automation or history is on, or the panel shows the clipboard, rows of permanent generators and effector rows are hidden from the grid. Rows of transient generators are hidden unless the widget is set to show them.

With a pinned item, on a transformable specification with automation off and the forest ready, the panel's root paths are all forest paths of that item. Root rows are the last rows of those paths. The normalized paths drop any path which continues a shorter one. Paths are recalculated 20 ms after each forest update only if the item was already pinned when the forest became ready; an item pinned later keeps its paths through forest updates (as the original does).
Pinning remembers the item, to focus it on the next restore; unpinning remembers the focused row. Toggling a pin also repaints rows of that item when it has duplicates.
Rows about to change flash only when the change is for the current specification and the forest has been ready for more than 1500 ms, so that the first load does not flash.

Rows can be dragged to move only if the panel is neither read-only nor locked, no dragged row is on a pinned root path, and, in a structure that requires parent edit permission, each row's parent is known to be editable. Rows can always be dragged to copy.

A drop is allowed when the panel is not read-only and there is a position. With a pin it must not be at the top level, with no paths, or above the last row of a path. The target parent must exist, must not be an automation row and, where parent edit permission is required, must be editable. The top level is refused if the panel has a title row. A drop from another panel is refused for rows not yet saved that have no item.

A row is known to be editable: always for temporary rows; never for loop marker rows; otherwise when the `editable` attribute is true. Callers may also accept the title row and non-issue rows, or any accessible row. A row is known not to be editable when that attribute is false.
The panel's title row is its first local row, if it has title semantics.

When a panel's state is restored the focus target is: the remembered row, else the first path of the remembered item, which is expanded, focused and scrolled to. With neither, the existing focus stays, or on the agile board tab focus is removed; elsewhere the first row is focused when nothing is. If no scroll position was restored the focused row is scrolled into view.
Dropping the specification cancels the forest subscription, unsyncs the row state, clears flash marks and gives the grid no forest.
While a panel shows the clipboard, attribute values are copied from the source for its rows, and again on every clipboard change.
After the forest loads, the panel follows the forest's stopped state, as other parts show it.
With 'Hide items that are not selected' on, rows not selected are filtered out, applied 150 ms after the switch; it is reapplied on selection changes not caused by the forest.

Duplicates controls are available on the board for a structure, or with no specification; not on the issue page, in gadgets or on the agile tab, and not for queries. When they become unavailable the duplicate icons and the footer's control are turned off. Availability is rechecked 50 ms after the structure changes.
The duplicates filter hides rows whose item appears once, keeping rows that are not regular items, computed from the unfiltered forest. Duplicate icons recreate the columns when toggled.

Statistics of the filtered forest are recomputed 50 ms after each update, and those of the whole forest likewise, but only while the duplicates filter is on, and when it is turned on. A new result of the filtered forest goes to the footer and is announced; the footer omits the duplicates count when duplicates are not available in the panel.
When the set of duplicated items changes, rows of those items repaint, and also when transforms get disabled or enabled.

Highlighting rows: the specification to highlight is the one set by search, or, without one and with automation off, the one derived from the panel's own specification. It subscribes to that forest and rows are matching if that forest contains them. With no such specification, there is no highlight. When that forest changes the highlight is refreshed 100 ms later.

Filtering rows by a set of items hides rows whose item is not in (or, in the opposite mode, is in) that set. Clipboard panels are not filtered, nor automation rows, nor rows not in the expanded forest. The set is re-read and the filter re-applied on the next tick after its forest changes.
When both an item filter and a highlight are active, a row counts as highlighted only if it passes both. The item filter is also applied as a filter of rows.
Callers can wait for the highlight forest's first answer, whether good or failed; with no highlight forest the request says so at once.
Finding the next matching row walks a given forest from a start index in a direction and returns the first index contained in the highlight forest, or -1, also -1 when no highlight forest exists.

Forest statistics count distinct items, skipping automation rows, loop markers and title rows. `itemsCount` is the number of distinct items, `duplicateItemsCount` the number appearing at least twice, `duplicateRowsCount` the rows those items take up. Example: items A, A, B, C, C, C give 3, 2, 5. With no forest all are 0.
Comparing statistics: with no earlier statistics all duplicated items count as changed. Otherwise an item is in the difference when its count differs from before.

A decision or error popup contributes height to the page layout only while it shows: its height minus the page header height. In a gadget its height is first divided by 0.75. The popup keeps its measured height until closed.
A popup's placement refreshes on page layout changes at most every 50 ms.

When an upload needs a decision or fails, the footer shows the warning 'Action is waiting for your decision' with the title 'Click to resolve conflict'; a click opens the popup. The popup opens at once unless the user is editing a cell. Only one action's popup exists: a new one replaces the old. An action without a result only re-shows the existing popup.
The popup sits above the footer warning, 500 px wide (400 px in a gadget), and opens after a 100 ms delay. Showing it when it is already open flashes it instead.
A decision left unanswered reopens or flashes the popup every 2 minutes, checked every second, except while the user is editing. A popup held back by editing opens within a second after editing ends.

The message states the action and the server's message: for a question '<action sentence> <server message>'; for an error '<server message> <action sentence>'. The action sentence uses the action's name, with the item's description as a link to `itemUrl` (`#` if none) and the number of other items, `itemCount` - 1: for example 'You are moving X.', 'You are moving X and one more item.', 'You are moving X and 3 more items.' for questions, and 'You were moving X.' for errors. The verbs are adding, copying, cutting, moving, removing.
For creating an item the sentence is 'You are about to create X.', or 'You have created X.' when the result has an item id, always in the question form, even on an error.
An action carrying a cut source reads as cutting, whatever its action name.

A plain click on the item link in the message, when the panel still shows the action's forest and has its row, expands the row's parents, scrolls to it and flashes it, and stays on the page. With another specification or no such row it also stays. A click with a modifier follows the link.

A result with `interactions` shows the first question. If its `parameter` is `0:Confirm` or `0:CreateAnyway` and it has one value, a single button labelled with that value's `message` is shown. Otherwise up to 3 values each get a button showing `iconHtml` and `message`; 4 or more give a drop-down of messages and a button 'Apply'. A 'Cancel' link is always there. Every value is offered, whether or not `possible` is true.
The drop-down reads only the first character of the selected option's index, so from the 11th value on it applies a wrong value (as the original does).

Choosing an answer stores it in the action's `parameters` under the question's `parameter` and removes the question. With more questions, the popup shows the next one; otherwise the action is retried with its answers.
'Cancel' on a question, or 'Acknowledge' on an error, cancels the edit of the action's temporary row, if any, and reports the failure as acknowledged to the upload queue.
A result with `error` and no questions shows the error's message and a button 'Acknowledge', with no options. Its row, item fields and count come from the error.
Closing a decision hides that action's footer warning, and, if it is the one in the popup, the popup and its reminder.

A panel has a banner area above the grid and one below it. Banners stack by an order number, lower first, and a later banner of equal order goes after. The area is hidden when no banner in it is visible.

A banner can have a hide button titled 'Hide' and a remove button titled 'Remove'; each appears only when given an action. Clicking one closes the banner and then runs the action, and does nothing else on the page.
A banner can be forced hidden: it then does not show while the force is on, however its toggle stands, and its height counts as 0.
A banner with a model key keeps its open state in the panel's stored UI state, under '<key>.<panel id>', default closed, saved as `true` or `false`.
The banner area's height is recalculated at most every 10 ms after a banner toggles, and is 0 while hidden.

The multi-selection banner, order 100 and with state key `ph.multi.selection`, opens when rows of the filtered forest are selected, and closes when none are. It reads '1 item selected' or 'N items selected'.
The banner's button 'Bulk Edit' ('Bulk change selected issues') is disabled unless Jira allows bulk change and the selection has at least two different issues. Clicking it runs bulk change.
The banner's toggle 'Filter' ('Hide items that are not selected') turns the hiding of unselected rows on and off.
The banner's button 'Planning task conversion' ('Convert selected planning tasks') is visible only when the selection has a planning task, and opens the conversion.
The banner's arrow buttons ('Go to next selected item', 'Go to previous selected item') focus the next or previous selected row, wrapping around; with only the focused row selected focus stays.
Closing the banner, by its button titled 'Clear selection' or by any other means, turns the filter off and clears the selection.
The banner's stored open state is restored when the panel asks for it.

With an empty query of type text or JQL the panel shows the banner 'Showing recent issues while the query is empty.'; with CQL 'Showing recent pages while the query is empty.'. The order is 4, the state key `ph.recent.items.warning`. It closes for any other specification.
With an empty S-JQL query the banner opens with no resolved text: it shows the message key itself (as the original does).

The panel header's right toolbar holds these buttons, with tooltip: run effectors 'Run all effectors in this structure', disabled at first; pin 'Pin focused item to show only its sub-items and parent items'; transformations 'Transformations – sort, filter, group or extend the displayed structure (without changing it)'; quick transformations 'Quick transformations'; search 'Search / filter the displayed structure'; a hidden two-panel mode button 'Hide items presented in the left panel. Currently showing all items.'; the view selector showing the view name and, for an unsaved adjustment, `*` titled 'You have adjusted this view and the changes have not been saved on the server yet.'. Pin, transformations, quick transformations and search are hidden on the agile tab and the issue page; the view selector on the agile tab.

The view selector's drop-down shows the current view's name; a search box with hint 'Search View'; 'Not found'; a progress spinner; lists headed 'Associated Views', 'Other Recent Views' and 'Views found:'; and the entry 'Manage Views...'.

The structure selector's menu has a search box 'Search Structure', a results list, the section 'Tools' with 'Text Search', 'JQL Query', 'Confluence Pages', 'Clipboard' with a size badge, and 'Current Project Issues', and a section with 'Manage Structure'. Beside it are a favourite star, a button 'Show structure description' and a lozenge 'archived', each hidden at first.

The search bar has a type button with the choices 'Text', 'JQL' and 'S-JQL', starting at 'Text'; a filter toggle 'Filter - don't show non-matching items'; a one-line query box; a link 'Save'; and an error place. The transformations bar has an add button titled 'Add structure transformation (it does not change how others see this structure)' with a menu of types.

The duplicates banner has a count label; 'Filter' ('Hide items that have no duplicates'); 'Pin' ('Pin selected item'); arrow buttons 'Next duplicate' and 'Previous duplicate'; and a checkbox 'Mark duplicate rows'.

Other banner layouts: generator information has an icon, a short text with an expand link, extra data, generator details and a button. A global error has an error icon and a message. The description banner has an info icon and content.
A drop-down's search box has the hint 'Search'.

On the issue page and the agile tab the toolbar has a hidden place button 'Insert current issue after the focused item in the structure', a pin button 'Pin current issue in the structure to show only its sub-items and parent items', and a menu: 'Add New…'; 'Expand all', 'Collapse all'; 'Edit', 'Copy', 'Cut', 'Paste', 'Remove'.
50 ms after a window rebuild, open cell editors are revalidated, and column autosizing is tried again after every rebuild and row repaint.
During a row drag the pointer's y is clamped to the viewport; the row is found from it by the current mode and limited to 0..rows, and the drop line is at that row x 33.
A header cell's focus, the autosize button's focus and the select-all mark's focus all turn off the whole widget's keyboard shortcuts, on all panels, until blur.
